gpu.title: GPU benchmark
gpu.subtitle: A Direct3D 11 game scene: a valley with 40,000 trees, real-time shadows, water and HDR. Same scene and camera on every PC.
gpu.window: The scene opens in its own window (Esc cancels). Sensor polling pauses during the test so it doesn't disturb the measurement; the first 3 seconds are warm-up and don't count.
gpu.ranking.empty: Results for this resolution and duration show up here. To compare with other PCs, import JSON reports on the Reports page.
stress.title: GPU stress test
stress.subtitle: A FurMark-style furry torus: maximum shader, overdraw and blending load to test temperatures, stability and the power supply.
stress.warning: This test pushes the graphics card to its power and temperature limits. Keep an eye on the readings and keep the automatic limit on.
stress.noSensor: There's no GPU temperature reading, so the automatic cutoff won't work. Continue anyway?
stress.status.running: Running. Esc in the test window also stops it.
stress.summary: {0} frames · average {1} FPS · max temperature {2} · duration {3}
cli.gpu.notWindows: GPU tests only work on Windows.
cli.usage:
Supernova Bench — command line

Usage:
  supernova-cli bench cpu [--mode multi|single|sustained] [--quick] [--threads N] [--minutes M] [--json] [--save] [--bmp file.bmp]
  supernova-cli bench gpu [--res 1080p|1440p|4k] [--seconds N] [--warp] [--headless]
  supernova-cli bench memory [--quick] [--json] [--save]
  supernova-cli bench disk [--drive C | --path FOLDER] [--size 256m|1g|4g] [--runs N] [--seconds S] [--json] [--save]
  supernova-cli stress cpu [--mode fma|render|int] [--threads N] [--seconds N]
  supernova-cli stress ram [--mb N | --percent P] [--seconds N]
  supernova-cli disk health
  supernova-cli games list [--json]
  supernova-cli gpu info
  supernova-cli info

Options:
  --quick     quick preset (480×270, 64 samples/pixel)
  --minutes   sustained mode duration (default 10)
  --json      print the result as JSON
  --save      store the result in the app history
  --warp      software GPU (WARP) with a reduced scene, for testing
  --lang      pt-BR or en
ranking.empty: Your results show up here. To compare with other PCs, import JSON reports on the Reports page.
report.memory: Read {0} GB/s · Write {1} GB/s · Latency {2} ns
mem.title: Memory and cache
mem.subtitle: RAM and L1/L2/L3 cache bandwidth and latency, AIDA64-style.
mem.hint: Takes about 30 seconds. Close games and heavy apps first; sensors are paused during the test.
mem.units: Read, write and copy in GB/s (all threads); latency in nanoseconds (one thread, random access).
mem.scoreHint: 1,000 points = a PC with dual-channel DDR4-3200. The score combines RAM read, write, copy and latency.
disk.title: Disk / SSD
disk.subtitle: Sequential and random read and write, CrystalDiskMark-style.
disk.hint: The test writes a temporary file to the drive (deleted at the end) and reads/writes straight to the disk, bypassing the Windows cache. Each full run writes a few GB to the SSD, which is normal and has no meaningful effect on its lifespan.
disk.error.space: Not enough free space for the {0} test file.
disk.scoreHint: 1,000 points = a typical SATA SSD. The score combines all 8 results; NVMe SSDs usually exceed 3,000.
health.title: Disk health
health.subtitle: SSD and HDD condition from SMART data, CrystalDiskInfo-style.
health.col.name: Attribute
health.footer: Good = no known problems. Caution = reallocated/pending sectors, errors or little remaining life: back up your data. Bad = the disk itself reports failure: back up now and replace it. Disks in RAID, on USB or with third-party drivers may not report SMART.
health.unavailable.admin: Run Supernova Bench as administrator to read this disk's SMART data.
health.unavailable.driver: This disk (or its driver/controller) doesn't report health data to Windows.
cpustress.title: CPU stress
cpustress.subtitle: Full load on every core, with a temperature limit and calculation error detection.
cpustress.warning: The processor will run hot and at full power. Use it to test cooling and stability (overclock/undervolt). The test stops by itself when it exceeds the temperature limit.
cpustress.mode.fma.desc: 256-bit vector FMA chains, like Linpack/Prime95 small FFT: maximum heat and power draw.
cpustress.mode.render.desc: The CPU benchmark renderer in a loop: a load similar to real rendering software.
cpustress.mode.int.desc: 64-bit integer multiplies and rotations: tests stability without the AVX power spike.
cpustress.stopOnError: Stop on the first calculation error
cpustress.noSensor: There's no CPU temperature reading, so the automatic cutoff won't work. Install PawnIO (notice above) to enable the sensor. Continue anyway?
cpustress.status.passed: Time completed with no calculation errors.
cpustress.status.stopped: Stopped by the user, no calculation errors.
cpustress.status.errors: {0} calculation error(s) (first on thread {1}): the CPU is unstable. Reduce the overclock/undervolt or raise the voltage.
cpustress.summary: Duration {0} · max temperature {1} · average clock {2} · errors {3}
ramstress.title: RAM test
ramstress.subtitle: Writes and verifies patterns across most free memory to find errors (TestMem5 / HCI MemTest-style).
ramstress.warning: Close games, browsers and other programs first: the test fills free memory and the PC may become slow. It can't reach memory already used by Windows; for a complete test outside Windows, use MemTest86.
ramstress.amount: How much to test (of free memory)
ramstress.verdict.failed: Failed: {0} error(s). The memory is unstable: lower the frequency/XMP/EXPO, loosen timings or test one stick at a time.
ramstress.verdict.incomplete: Time completed with {0} coverage and no errors.
ramstress.verdict.stopped: Stopped by the user at {0} coverage with no errors.
ramstress.oom: Couldn't reserve that much memory. Choose a lower percentage or close other programs.
ramstress.footer: Positions are counted from the start of the tested area. A single error already means instability.
